name: TXS0102DQER
title: TXS0102: 2-bit bidirectional voltage-level translator, auto direction, open-drain and push-pull
summary: A two-channel, non-inverting level translator with no direction pin: each channel works out on its own which side is driving. The A side runs from VCCA, 1.65 V to 3.6 V, and the B side from VCCB, 2.3 V to 5.5 V, with VCCA no higher than VCCB. Each channel is an N-channel pass transistor with a 10 kΩ pull-up on each side and one-shot circuits that speed up rising edges, so it suits open-drain buses such as I2C and SMBus as well as push-pull signals. OE low, or either supply at ground, puts both sides in high impedance.
key_figures: 10 kΩ per I/O, to VCCA or VCCB
±2500 V A port, ±8000 V B port
SSOP-8 (DCT), VSSOP-8 (DCU), X2SON-8 (DQE, DQM), X1SON-8 (DTT), DSBGA-8 (YZP)

notes: Where several markings are given in parentheses, any one of them may appear on the part.
An automotive-qualified version is offered as TXS0102-Q1.

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: A 1.8 V controller talks to a 3.3 V system over two data lines. The controller's 1.8 V rail feeds VCCA, the system's 3.3 V rail feeds VCCB, and the controller drives OE. A1 and A2 join the controller's data pins, B1 and B2 the system's. C1 bypasses the 1.8 V rail; C2 and C3 bypass the 3.3 V rail. All three share one ground.
notes: Design example: input range 1.65 V to 3.6 V, output range 2.3 V to 5.5 V, with VCCA ≤ VCCB.

circuits.title: Layout example parts
circuits.description: The parts placed round a TXS0102DCTR in the board example. A 0.1 µF capacitor sits across VCCA and GND at pins 3 and 2, another 0.1 µF from VCCB, pin 7, to the ground plane, and a resistor pulls OE, pin 6, to ground so the outputs stay off until both supplies are up. B1 and B2 run to the system, A1 and A2 to the controller.
notes: The OE pull-down's least value is set by how much current the driver of OE can source.

circuits.description: A pulse generator drives one input of the part directly; the matching output carries 15 pF and 1 MΩ to ground. Used for data rate, pulse width, propagation delay, rise and fall time with a push-pull driver.

equations.name: Output high level with an external pull-down

where.VCCx: supply of that side, VCCA or VCCB

equations.note: A pull-down on an I/O lowers both VOH and VOL.

operation.text: Each channel is an N-channel pass transistor between A and B with a 10 kΩ pull-up on each side. Its gate bias sits roughly one threshold voltage above the lower of the two supplies. Data may move either way, and each I/O becomes an input or an output as needed, without a control line.

One-shot circuits on both sides watch for a rising edge. When one arrives they switch on PMOS transistors (T1, T2) that bypass the pull-ups, for about 30 ns or 95 % of the edge, whichever ends sooner; meanwhile the output resistance falls to roughly 50 Ω to 70 Ω. A signal in the other direction should wait until the one-shot has turned off, to limit dynamic ICC and contention; the longest this takes equals the minimum pulse duration tw.

Steady low-level current is sunk by the external open-drain or push-pull driver. The part sources only a few hundred µA of dc current, through its 10 kΩ pull-ups. Fall times, tPHL and maximum data rate depend on the external driver's edge rate and output impedance and on line capacitance; the specified tfA, tfB, tPHL and data rates take a driver impedance below 50 Ω.

Keep traces short so a reflection's round trip ends within the one-shot time (about 30 ns), when the source is still low impedance. The capacitance the part can drive is set by that duration: with a very heavy load the one-shot ends before the line reaches the upper rail. Trace and connector capacitance both count, and too much can cause one-shot retriggering, bus contention or ringing.

OE low disables the part and floats every I/O; OE high enables it. tdis runs from OE falling to the outputs going high impedance; ten is the time the one-shots need to start working after OE rises. The internal pull-ups are switched off while OE is low. OE is powered from VCCA.

A-side I/Os have 10 kΩ to VCCA and B-side I/Os 10 kΩ to VCCB. A stronger pull-up is an external resistor from the I/O to its supply, in parallel with the internal one; a lower pull-up value affects VOL. External pull-ups can cut the RC time of a line; a pull-down lowers VOH as the equation gives.

VCCA must stay at or below VCCB throughout operation. Either supply may come up first without harm. To hold the outputs in high impedance while power is applied or removed, pull OE to GND with a resistor and leave it low until both supplies are settled; the driver's sourcing ability sets the smallest resistor. If either supply is at ground, both sides go high impedance.

Partial-power-down operation is supported; Ioff is specified with either supply at 0 V. Latch-up is rated above 100 mA (JESD 78, Class II). ESD per JESD 22: A side 2500 V HBM (A114-B), 250 V machine model (A115-A), 1500 V CDM (C101); B side 8 kV HBM, 250 V machine model, 1500 V CDM.

Meant for point-to-point links between circuits on different logic supplies, chiefly bidirectional open-drain lines with no direction signal, such as I2C, SMBus or 1-wire; also UART and GPIO. Push-pull drivers work too, though TI points to the TXB0102 for push-pull use. The levels 1.8 V, 2.5 V, 3.3 V and 5 V can all be bridged.
The driving device's supply sets the input range: its high level has to exceed VIH of the input side and its low level stay below VIL. The supply of the device being driven sets the output range.

Each supply gets a bypass capacitor placed right at its VCCA or VCCB pin and the GND pin. Signal traces stay short to limit loading and so that reflections return within the roughly 30 ns one-shot time.

Input pulses come from a generator with PRR 10 MHz, ZO = 50 Ω and dv/dt ≥ 1 V/ns, one transition per measurement. Timing is taken at VCCI / 2 on the input and VCCO / 2 on the output; rise and fall times between 0.1 and 0.9 of VCCO. Enable and disable times start at OE crossing VCCA / 2. tPZL ends at 0.1 × VCCO and tPZH at 0.9 × VCCO; tPLZ and tPHZ end at VCCO / 2. S1 is at 2 × VCCO for tPZL and tPLZ and open for tPHZ and tPZH.
